data.name: Puran
data.gender_notes: Puran is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Puran is a name derived from the Sanskrit word ‘purana’ which means ancient, old, and wise. It is a name that signifies a deep understanding of the world and the wisdom that comes with age. The name Puran carries the meaning “Ancient, Wise” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit, Hindi. Parents who choose Puran usually hope their child will grow to embody ancient, wise and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Puran is a name that reflects the deep spiritual understanding of the ancient Hindu sages. It is a name that carries the power of knowledge, wisdom, and the deep connection with the divine.
data.etymology: Puran belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ancient, Wise.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Puran total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Puran holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism and is often associated with ancient wisdom and knowledge. In Hindu scriptures, there are numerous works of literature known as Puranas. These texts not only serve as historical records but also contain moral and spiritual teachings that continue to be relevant today. The name Puran carries the influence of these ancient texts, symbolizing the carrier of valuable knowledge and traditions.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Puran represents an individual who embodies timeless knowledge and wisdom. It represents one who has transcended the trials and tribulations of life and has deep insights into the workings of the universe. The name Puran can also be seen as a reminder to seek knowledge, listen to wisdom, and grow spiritually. In the Hindu tradition, the name Puran is also believed to bring blessings of long life and prosperity.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Puran signifies the accumulation of wisdom and knowledge over many lifetimes. It embodies the idea of continual learning and growth through experience. The name Puran is a reminder to remain open to new insights and perspectives, and to carry the lessons of the past into the present.

historical_references.reference: The Mahabharata is one of the two major Sanskrit epics of ancient India, the other being the Ramayana. It is an epic poem that narrates the Kurukshetra war between two branches of the Kuru family, the Pandavas and the Kauravas, over the throne of Hastinapura. The Mahabharata is estimated to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE. Puran, one of the five Pandava brothers, is a significant character in this epic.

Another reference to Puran can be found in the 13th century Hindu text, the Bhagavata Purana. This text is a collection of stories about the avatars of the god Vishnu, and is considered one of the most important texts in the Vaishnavism tradition. The Bhagavata Purana is estimated to have been written between the 10th and 13th centuries CE. In this text, Puran is mentioned as a sage and a devotee of Vishnu.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Puran' has been modernly interpreted as a reference to the ancient Hindu texts known as the 'Puranas'. These texts are a rich source of Indian culture, history, and spiritual teachings. In contemporary times, there has been a significant surge in interest in these texts, leading to their exploration on various platforms. On YouTube, numerous channels and videos exist that delve into the stories and teachings of the Puranas. Podcasts, too, have gained popularity as a medium to discuss and explore these texts in-depth. Additionally, numerous mobile applications have been developed to make the Puranas more accessible, offering features such as audio books, interactive quizzes, and multimedia presentations.

name_in_real_life.story: Maya Puran, a teacher in Kolkata, India, shares that their name Puran meaning "Ancient, Wise" has been a constant source of inspiration, motivating them to follow Hindu values and serve their community.
